references.text: The seraphs cry out that the whole earth is full of the Lord's glory, reflecting the promise in Numbers 14:21 that the Lord's glory will fill the whole earth.
The prophecy that the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord as the waters cover the sea is thematically linked to the promise that the Lord's glory will fill the earth.
Habakkuk repeats almost word for word the promise from Numbers 14:21 that the earth shall be filled with knowledge of the Lord's glory.
The psalm praises the Lord's glorious name and expresses the desire that the whole earth be filled with his glory, as a prayer for the fulfillment of the promise in Numbers.
Ezekiel prophesies that the Lord's glory will be made known among the nations, connecting to the theme of God's glory filling the earth.
God confirms his oath with the expression 'as surely as I live,' the same formula used in verse 21.
God swears by himself using the expression 'as surely as I live,' the same oath formula as in Numbers 14:21.
The Lord uses the oath 'as surely as I live' to confirm his word, the same formula as in Numbers 14:21.
